detail.longDescription: This is my Python Dataframe A B C D 0 0.10 NaN -0.05 NaN 1 0.03 0.12 NaN NaN 2 -0.06 NaN 0.03 NaN 3 NaN NaN 0.07 0.11 I would like to remove the NaN values ​​and reduce the dataframe, keeping in mind that the number of non-NaN values ​​is always constant in each row—in this case, 2—and that I want to preserve the consecutive sequences within each column (for example, (0.10, 0.03, -0.06) from column A and (0.03, 0.07) from column C). The desired result is as follows: E F 0 0.10 -0.05 1 0.03 0.12 2 -0.06 0.03 3 0.11 0.07 If possible, I would like to preserve the association between the values ​​in new dataframe and the original columns. For example, -0.06 belonged to A, and 0.12 belonged to B. How can I do this? Setup: df = pd.DataFrame({ 'A': [0.10, 0.03, -0.06, np.nan], 'B': [np.nan, 0.12, np.nan, np.nan], 'C': [-0.05, np.nan, 0.03, 0.07], 'D': [np.nan, np.nan, np.nan, 0.11] })
